title: China’s AI infrastructure boom fuels earnings surge for local chip firms
source_used: BigGo Finance roundup of 16 Oct 2026 (SCMP article not readable)
key_facts: On 16 Oct 2026 a dense wave of Chinese A-share tech earnings pre-announcements and buyback disclosures came out.

Longsys (memory chip maker) projected first-three-quarters net profit of 14 billion to 14.9 billion yuan, up 1,864.55 to 1,990.84 percent; it noted that the marginal contribution of rising memory prices to profit has slowed significantly.
Hygon (domestic AI chip company) projected net profit of 2.71 billion to 2.98 billion yuan, up 38.16 to 51.93 percent.
MetaX (domestic AI chip company) swung to a profit, projecting 587 million to 717 million yuan.
Sugon reported first-three-quarters revenue of 12.238 billion yuan, up 38.75 percent, and net profit of 1.724 billion yuan, up 78.48 percent.
Several firms also announced buybacks, for example Eoptolink (800 million to 1 billion yuan) and Piotech (200 million to 300 million yuan).
SCMP headline (not read): China's AI infrastructure boom and self-sufficiency push fuel an earnings surge for local chip firms.
quote_evidence: Longsys projected its first-three-quarters net profit to surge more than 18-fold year-on-year, while Han's CNC, Sugon, Hygon and several other companies also reported substantial profit growth.

Among Chinese domestic AI chip companies, Hygon (688041.SS) projected first-three-quarters net profit of 2.71 billion to 2.98 billion yuan (approximately $405.6 million to $446.0 million), up 38.16% to 51.93%.
MetaX (688802.SS) swung to profitability, projecting net profit of 587 million to 717 million yuan (approximately $87.9 million to $107.3 million).
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese chip suppliers are reporting strong profits from domestic AI spending, but the numbers are company projections.
notes: SCMP article (HTTP 403) not opened. The facts come from a BigGo Finance roundup of the 16 Oct company announcements; SCMP's framing is taken from its headline and link only. Cambricon and others named in the SCMP piece, if any, are not covered here.
